subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where `sender` canonicalizes to `destination_caller_id`, should OpenClaw repair only confidently recovered canonical peers and drop ambiguous payloads before access control?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, direct-session routing, and reply delivery, so it is an identity-boundary decision beyond a mechanical refactor.

options.title: Repair Canonical Peers And Fail Closed
options.body: Use canonical handle normalization, repair only when a distinct peer is recovered, and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control while requiring live after-fix proof.

options.title: Repair Only And Preserve Current Fallthrough
options.body: Normalize the repair but allow unrepaired ambiguous payloads to continue into existing access-control behavior, accepting the residual identity risk.

options.title: Pause For Root-Cause Clarification
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is not this sender-fallback race, pause or close this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Canonical Peers And Fail Closed
recommendation.body: Use canonical handle normalization, repair only when a distinct peer is recovered, and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control while requiring live after-fix proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged destination_caller_id self-chat work established the closest current invariant this decision builds on.
